done_when: After a plan's latest read round passed, edits only below '## For the builders' need no new read (as they need no new approval): forge next, approval and task start accept them. An edit to the top part (title down to For the builders) still needs a round, and that round's prompt asks the reader to check only the diff and the sections it touches. Command-level tests: a builders-only edit after a pass (no round needed), a top-part edit after a pass (round needed, prompt names the diff and touched sections).

findings.body: After the first task merges, edit the plan's Why, pass another read, then commit a builders-only edit and start a later task. The Why edit leaves the approval hash unchanged, so no renewed approval pushes the story branch; the passing read only commits locally (story.py:279–281 and repo.py:457–468). Later tasks start from main and copy the current plan, notes and state without the story history (task.py:143–147, 186–187 and 119–121). Consequently, pushing that task need not transmit the earlier plan blob named by read_hash. In a fresh CI checkout, this cat-file fails and the pull-request check incorrectly demands another read for the builders-only edit. Ensure the passing baseline is available from the pushed task, and cover this later-task carry scenario.
findings.title: Preserve the read baseline when carrying a plan into a later task

why: After a plan read passes, any later edit, even a one-line wording change, costs a full new read round of about ten minutes before the plan can be approved or its next task started
